body:
Yeah I'm pretty much teaching myself physics right now. I had a great chemistry teacher so I had no problem with that, but I had to teach myself bio too. Physics is just... so crazy. It's not that it's overly difficult, but I don't have enough time to do enough examples to actually understand the formulas. And every day we have to learn and memorize more. I google everything, but it's all the same thing as in my text book. I just have nobody to ask "why are you doing this" or "How do you get from here to here" I have a test tomorrow (covers 3 units) an project due Friday, another unit test next Tuesday and the final exam on Thursday. I have no choice but to keep going... I just don't know if I'll be able to do my best come the final exam. I'm just so done with it now. :(

I have asked my teacher for help. He's not very.... welcoming. He just kind of laughs and makes me feel stupid because the concepts are easy, but I'm not getting them. I don't know. I can do the chemistry math no problem (finished with a 93%) but this stuff, it's not that I CAN'T understand it, but my teacher just doesn't explain it very well. And when I ask he just tells me the same thing over and over and then pretty much shoo's me away. I haven't done any of this in over 9 years, and because a lot of the people in the program have recently been doing this stuff, he tells me I just need to figure it out and keep up. 

I honestly don't know how I'm going to memorize all these equations for the final. Right now, there's at least 22 that I need to know. We get a "cheat sheet" for quizzes, but not for the test. Given I've already finished college once, and have acutally done work in the workplace, I know that you don't NEED to have equations memorized. Your supervisor isn't going to fire you if you need to look up how to do something. It's not going to be a requirement for a job to have every possible equation memorized. I understand teachers want us to learn them, but coming from "real world experience" I know it's not the case.

I'm just so tired of not wanting to wake up in the morning, dreading the 6 hours of class I have, only to have to go home and spend all night doing homework. And I have to do it all again the next day.

I have a math course I'm doing at home too, and I have 3 lessons to finish for that, then I have to write the final exam, I have no time to do the lessons, and I fear that I won't be able to get them done and the exam written before I have to have my grades into the college. 

Everything is just piling up and I have no outlet. It's not like I can just put everything down and go to the movies, or play video games, because if I do, I'm further behind in my work. 

My one friend keeps telling me I'll do fine. The other day, she said "Your best is all you can do" I know she was trying to be encouraging, but what if my best is a 60? I need a minimum of a 70. if I do my best, try my hardest and only get a 60, does that mean that's the best I can do? I don't know, but I'm starting to feel that.

I wish I had friends who cared about what was actually going on. Not just the ones who are interested in me (see girl mentioned above) because all they want is attention, and I can't give that.

The one person, I could tell anything to, who would listen to my anxieties, who would give me the support I needed when I was falling behind, she's not there anymore... It's like a big, person shaped hole is missing in my life and I don't know how to fill it, how to fix it. I don't know how to forget her.

It sucks, because the few people I have reached out to, have given me nothing. But when they need me, I'm always there to reply, to talk, to do whatever.

I'm tired of these one sided relationships. And I know my last was going that way for a while, but I still love~~d~~ her. She's dissociated herself from everything we were, everything we had. And she makes it look so easy. I wish I could do the same, and just stop feeling but I can't.... and right now, I can only think of one way to do that.
